probe: ticket 0025 X4 — json_each-constrained MATCH cost by rowid-set scope, on a synthetic 477k corpus
rule: DESIGN.md §3 X4: ladder step at the largest scope with constrained-MATCH p95 <= 150 ms; if even 1k exceeds it, no constrained step ships
substrate: REAL corpus at /home/haduong/data/projets/zoteus-bench/x2-rebuild/search-index.sqlite: 477512 passages of the author's own library, probed with terms drawn from ITS OWN vocabulary via fts5vocab, one per df band (>=10%, 0,1-1%, <0,1%). The synthetic vocabulary is NOT used here: its terms are near-absent from a real index, so they would answer in about a millisecond and, X4 being an upper bound, read as a pass.

vocabulary.source: fts5vocab(main, passages_fts, row) on the index under test

scopes_note: 20k and 100k were deliberately NOT run. The rule turns on the SMALLEST scope — if even 1k exceeds the allowance no constrained step ships — and 1k exceeds it by 80x, so the verdict is settled. The larger rungs would only draw a curve already shown to be superlinear (5x the scope costs 7,5x the median), at a p95 of 74,6 s per probe at 5k and worse above.
verdict: NO CONSTRAINED STEP SHIPS, confirmed on the real corpus. At a 1000-rowid scope the constrained p95 is 11 969,6 ms against the 150 ms allowance, and the constrained median (585,7 ms) is 8x the cost of ranking the whole 477 512-passage corpus unconstrained (73,6 ms). The synthetic arm reached the same verdict; this is its confirmation on real text and a real vocabulary.
